events.summary: S&P Dow Jones Indices said FormFactor moves from the S&P SmallCap 600 into the S&P MidCap 400, replacing Twilio (which moves up into the S&P 500 in place of Warner Bros. Discovery). Effective before the open on Monday 2026-10-06. Workiva takes FormFactor's SmallCap 600 seat. The release gives no reason beyond the chain of replacements. A contemporaneous post quoting the release shows FORM at 148.44, its 2026-10-01 close, which places the announcement after Thursday's close.
events.why_it_matters: This is a promotion to a bigger-company index because the company has grown (market value about $11.65B per a tier-3 quote page, not independently confirmed). Funds that track the MidCap 400 must buy, and funds that track the SmallCap 600 must sell, so the net effect on demand is unclear. Index rebalancing usually happens at the close before the effective date, which here is Friday 2026-10-02 (inference). It changes nothing about the business itself.

events.summary: BACKGROUND. Deutsche Bank (analyst George Brown) started covering FormFactor with a Buy rating and a $200 price target. The note's central claim is that FormFactor has become the second qualified supplier of probe cards for Nvidia GPUs made at TSMC. DB says this market is worth about $0.5B, expects first sales in the second half of 2026, and sees roughly 20% share and more than $0.2B of sales by 2028. DB also sees HBM-related sales approaching $0.4B by 2028. FORM rose 9.6% that day (136.25 to 149.31, local data) while SMH rose only 0.35% (606.90 to 609.00), so almost all of the move was company-specific.
events.why_it_matters: This is the single biggest company-specific move of the past week, and it explains most of the 15% weekly gain. The price target and the 2028 sales numbers are one analyst's opinions. FormFactor itself has not named Nvidia. On its Q2 call it said only that it is 'qualified' and 'shipping production units for revenue' in GPU probe cards in Q3.

events.summary: BACKGROUND. Q2 2026 brought record results. Revenue was $258.2M, up 14.2% from Q1's $226.1M and up 31.9% from $195.8M a year earlier. Non-GAAP gross margin was 53.3% (38.5% a year earlier) and non-GAAP EPS was $0.82 ($0.27 a year earlier); GAAP EPS was $0.71. All three beat the top of the company's own range. Q3 guidance: revenue $270M +/- $10M, non-GAAP gross margin 54.0% +/- 1.5pts, non-GAAP EPS $0.86 +/- $0.09. Consensus had been about $240M revenue (Zacks) and $0.59-$0.61 EPS (sources differ). The stock jumped 26.3% the next day (83.45 to 105.38) while SMH rose 6.9%.
events.why_it_matters: It showed that the AI story (HBM memory testing, GPU and custom-chip testing, and optics test systems) is turning into actual revenue and much higher margins. Management attributed about one third of the Q2 margin improvement to items that will not repeat (tariff refunds, precious-metal reclaim).

events.summary: BACKGROUND. FORM fell 16.0% on the day (147.13 to 123.59, local data; StockStory reported 17.5%). This was part of a chip-sector selloff over fears that AI chip demand may be cooling. A Citi analyst questioned whether cloud giants would keep spending heavily on AI if they could not show returns, and Meta's plan to lease out spare AI computing capacity raised fears of overbuilding. SMH fell 4.5% that day (local data). The slide continued to $83.45 on 2026-07-29, about 48% below the $160.27 intraday high of 2026-06-30, before earnings reversed it.
events.why_it_matters: It shows how violently this stock reacts to any doubt about AI spending. Its beta (how much it tends to move when the market moves) is 2.82, and its 60-day volatility is 95.7% a year. A 1-month gain of 54% sits inside a 1-year range in which the stock also fell 48% from peak to trough.

events.summary: BACKGROUND (industry). Micron reported fiscal Q4 revenue of $54.23B against $51.07B expected, and adjusted EPS of $33.42 against $31.61 expected. Its DRAM revenue rose 343% from a year earlier to $39.8B, and it cited a strong HBM roadmap. The figures come from a search summary of CNBC; the CNBC page returned an error, and the Micron 8-K was not opened.
events.why_it_matters: DRAM, and especially HBM, is FormFactor's largest end market: HBM was about two-thirds of FormFactor's DRAM revenue in Q2. Memory makers' results are a read-through for FormFactor's probe-card demand. SK hynix was 24.3% of FormFactor's Q2 revenue.

why_chain.text: FORM rose 54.4% in one month (about $96.58 on 2026-09-02 to $149.15 on 2026-10-02), versus about +14.6% for the chip ETF SMH (550.48 to 630.60). So most of the month's move was company-specific (excess vs sector, 1m: +39.9 pts). In the last week (+15.0%), the attribution model gives +8.6% to industry and +6.4% to the company.
The largest single company-specific day was 2026-09-30 (+9.6% vs SMH +0.35%), when Deutsche Bank started coverage with Buy and a $200 target.
DB's reason: FormFactor is now the second qualified probe-card supplier for Nvidia GPUs made at TSMC (about a $0.5B market per DB), and its HBM test business keeps growing.

The company's own facts back the direction. It said it is 'qualified' and 'shipping production units for revenue' in GPU probe cards in Q3 2026, without naming the customer. It also reported record Q2 revenue and margins and guided Q3 to another record ($270M midpoint).

Root driver: AI chips (GPUs, custom accelerators) and the HBM memory stacked beside them are expensive and complex, so every chip must be tested on the wafer before packaging. That raises demand for advanced probe cards. Cloud companies' AI spending is the money at the bottom of the chain.

Part of the September rebound was simply recovery from an oversold base. The stock had fallen to about $95 on 2026-09-01 amid general chip-stock weakness, and the gains from 2026-09-04 to 2026-09-23 (about $96.76 to $131.26) have no single published company-specific reason that I found. Memory-sector strength ahead of Micron's 2026-09-30 report is a plausible contributor.
why_chain.evidence: inference (medium); no published cause found for the 2026-09-04 to 2026-09-23 leg

products.name: Probe cards (DRAM/HBM, foundry and logic incl. GPU and custom ASIC)
products.what_it_is: A custom-made test head with thousands of microscopic needles that touches every chip while the chips are still on the silicon wafer, to check which ones work before they are cut out and packaged.
products.analogy: A bed of nails built to fit one specific chip design. It presses down on the wafer like a cookie-cutter shaped stethoscope and listens to every chip at once. A new chip design needs a new card, and cards wear out, so customers keep buying.
products.buyers: Memory makers (SK hynix was 24.3% of Q2 2026 revenue), foundries (TSMC was 11.0%), and chip designers such as Intel. Per Deutsche Bank, Nvidia GPUs made at TSMC are now included.
products.how_it_works: A tester sends electrical signals through the card's probes into each chip's contact pads on the wafer, then reads the responses. Bad chips are marked and discarded before expensive packaging. That matters most for HBM, where many memory dies are stacked together and one bad die ruins the whole stack, and for big AI chips.
products.sales: Segment revenue for Q2 2026 is not disclosed in the release text (posted separately on the IR site; not retrieved). Total company revenue was $258.2M, of which the Systems segment was $48.5M (per the call), which implies about $209.7M from Probe Cards (my arithmetic). HBM was about two-thirds of DRAM probe-card revenue. GPU probe cards: 'shipping production units for revenue' starting Q3 2026; amount not disclosed. Deutsche Bank estimates more than $0.2B of GPU probe-card sales by 2028 and about $0.4B of HBM sales by 2028 (analyst estimates, not company figures).
products.stage: HBM/DRAM: shipping in volume. GPU probe cards: qualified and shipping first production units (Q3 2026).
products.size_for_company: Probe cards are roughly 80% of revenue (proxy: $209.7M of $258.2M in Q2 2026, derived). If DB's more than $0.2B GPU estimate for 2028 came true, it would be about 19% of 2026 consensus revenue of $1.03B (stockanalysis.com consensus).
products.competition: Technoprobe (Italy) and Micronics Japan (MJC) are the main probe-card rivals. Per DB, FormFactor is the second source at Nvidia/TSMC, so a competitor is the primary supplier (not named in the sources I read).
products.why_investors_care: Each new AI chip or HBM generation needs new, more complex and pricier cards. Being a qualified second source at the biggest AI chip customer opens a new revenue stream.
products.watch_next: Q3 results (est. 2026-10-28): GPU revenue disclosure, DRAM mix shift from HBM to DDR (management flagged it), and Q4 guidance.

products.name: Co-packaged optics (CPO) test systems (Systems segment)
products.what_it_is: Precision test stations that check chips which combine electronics and laser-light (optical) connections in one package, the kind of parts used to link AI servers with light instead of copper.
products.analogy: A quality-control bench for a new kind of hybrid part, half electronic chip and half fibre-optic plug, that must be checked with both electricity and light before it ships.
products.buyers: Makers and developers of silicon photonics and CPO devices for AI data-center networking (customer names not disclosed).
products.how_it_works: Systems (probe stations) hold the wafer or device in place under precise temperature and alignment while electrical and optical signals are applied. FormFactor's Keystone Photonics acquisition added CPO and silicon-photonics test capability.
products.sales: Systems segment revenue was $48.5M in Q2 2026, up 74% from Q1 (call). CPO revenue for 2026 was originally guided at $10-20M; management now expects to 'significantly exceed the $20 million level for the year overall'.
products.size_for_company: More than $20M a year would be about 2% of 2026 consensus revenue ($1.03B): small today, but an option on optical AI networking.
products.competition: not available from sources read (test-equipment peers in photonics test exist; not verified)
products.why_investors_care: It ties FormFactor to the next AI networking shift (CPO), which other holdings in the portfolio are also exposed to.
products.watch_next: An updated 2026 CPO revenue figure on the Q3 call.
